long_biography.plain_text:
After graduating from ESSEC, Petithuguenin worked in construction as a controller, finance director and general manager. He later joined Compagnie Générale des Eaux, eventually leading its recycling and industrial-cleaning activities. In 1994 he bought Paprec, then a 45-person paper-and-cardboard recycler in La Courneuve, and made it the basis of a new family-controlled group.

Petithuguenin combined organic expansion with targeted acquisitions, broadening Paprec into waste collection, recycling, treatment and energy recovery across multiple countries. He also made diversity, secularism and social inclusion explicit themes of the company's management culture. The Petithuguenin family retained majority ownership while outside investors supplied growth capital. He progressively handed French and international management to his sons, retiring in 2025 after more than three decades.
